title: Lockheed Will Pay $29.5 Million Over Claims It Discriminated Against White Employees
detail:
Lockheed Will Pay $29.5 Million Over Claims It Discriminated Against White Employees

Quick Read

Lockheed Martin (LMT) agreed to pay $29.5 million to settle federal claims of race discrimination and false civil rights certifications as a government contractor.

IBM (IBM) at $17 million and Accenture Federal Services (ACN) at $25 million faced similar 2026 settlements, making Lockheed the DOJ's fourth such case.

The $29.5 million settlement equals about 1.6% of Lockheed's Q3 net earnings of $1.8 billion, making it financially insignificant to shareholders.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

On November 3, 2026, the Justice Department and the EEOC announced that Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) agreed to pay $29.5 million. The payment settles allegations of employment discrimination and allegations that Lockheed falsely certified, as a federal contractor, that it complied with federal civil rights laws.

Kevin Moloney / Getty Images

The money is split two ways. $22 million goes to the United States under the False Claims Act, a law that lets the government recover money from contractors over false claims. That part covers alleged race- and sex-based employment practices from 2019 to the present.

About $7.5 million goes to more than a thousand employees through the EEOC. It settles a 2025 Commissioner's Charge filed by EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, which alleged race discrimination against white employees in performance reviews, bonuses and other pay.

The DOJ said the claims are "allegations only and there has been no determination of liability" and that "Lockheed cooperated in the resolution of these matters." The stock fell 0.59% in the regular session and traded at $639.33 at 7:58 p.m. ET. No public source has tied that move to the settlement.

LMT Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
What the Justice Department Alleges

The False Claims Act portion settles a whistleblower suit that former Lockheed Vice President Tim Booher filed in the Northern District of Texas. "Under this resolution, Mr. Booher will receive $4,400,000," the DOJ said.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock rose 120.6% in the twelve months to November 3, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 11.8%. In a September 2, 2026 report during that period, management raised its outlook for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 after record orders. How much of that rise came from a bigger business, and how much from a higher price for each dollar of sales? The short answer is mostly the price, while HPE's twelve-month margin is back at its 2024 level.

How Much Of HPE's Rise Came From Its Sales?

HPE's revenue grew 26.6% over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, reaching $41.9 billion. That growth was far less than the advance in its stock. Most of the rise came from buyers paying more for each dollar of sales.

That price is the price-to-sales ratio, which measures what buyers pay for the entire company against what it sells in a year. A company whose sales stay flat, for example, doubles in value if its ratio goes from one to two.

HPE's ratio climbed from 0.8 at the end of June 2025 to 1.4 at the end of June 2026. That marked its highest reading in quarterly data going back to fiscal 2016.

How Did HPE's Business Change In A Year?

HPE's operating margin rose in each of the three quarters following fiscal Q4 2025, when it stood at 4.2%. It reached 6.3% in fiscal Q1 2026 and 7.7% in fiscal Q2 2026.

In fiscal Q3 2026, the operating margin reached 12.0%, compared with 4.7% in fiscal Q3 2025. Revenue for that quarter was $12.2 billion, up 33.7% from a year earlier. Management said some of its figures are normalized to include Juniper Networks results from the start of fiscal 2025. The figures in this article are as reported in company filings, not management's adjusted figures.

Management reported that quarter on September 2, 2026. It said the company booked more orders than in any prior quarter, leaving a record backlog, and that supply constraints were still holding back its ability to meet the higher demand. Management raised its outlook for both fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, and it now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 13% to 17%.

HPE's Twelve-Month Margin Is Back At Its 2024 Level

Over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, HPE's operating margin was 7.8%, matching its level over the twelve months to July 31, 2024. Its highest twelve-month level at any quarter end since fiscal 2016 was 8.9%, recorded in fiscal Q2 2023.

So the price you pay for each dollar of HPE's sales climbed to the top of its range, while its twelve-month margin stayed inside its own. At the November 3, 2026 close, the ratio was 1.7, exceeding its June 2026 reading. You now pay 25.4 times HPE's earnings, compared with 22.8 for the S&P 500. The shares have already fallen 22.3% from October 5 to November 3, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 2.6%.

title: IBM Plummets 18.5% in the Past Year: Time to Reassess the Stock?

IBM Plummets 18.5% in the Past Year: Time to Reassess the Stock?

ANTH.PVT

Trading disclosure

International Business Machines Corporation IBM has declined 18.5% over the past year against the industry's growth of 81.3% due to macroeconomic challenges and a potent threat from AI firm Anthropic that threatens its core legacy businesses. The stock has lagged peers like Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN. While Microsoft has gained 2.2%, Amazon has remained flat on average over this period.

One-Year IBM Stock Price Performance

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Ails IBM?

IBM has long positioned itself as the dominant provider of mainframe systems optimized for high-volume, mission-critical workloads characterized by AI. Over decades, the company has built a durable revenue stream around maintaining, upgrading and modernizing legacy COBOL environments for large enterprises. The complexity of COBOL systems has historically served as a competitive moat. Many organizations hesitate to rewrite or replace these systems due to cost, operational risk and the shrinking pool of developers familiar with the language. But it appears that the moat may now be facing AI-driven erosion.

Anthropic's Claude Code tool can reportedly modernize legacy COBOL systems — a foundational programming language deeply embedded in IBM's mainframe ecosystem. With Claude Code proposing to substantially automate code exploration, documentation, refactoring and security analysis, it threatens to reduce enterprises' reliance on specialized legacy service providers like IBM, putting its sustenance at stake. COBOL remains deeply embedded in global infrastructure and continues to run in production daily across financial institutions, airlines, retailers and government systems. If Claude Code meaningfully reduces the cost and complexity of analyzing and migrating legacy systems, it could compress pricing power in IBM's Consulting segment, introducing a new competitive dynamic into a space that has historically been a labor-intensive and high-margin business for the company.

Margin Woes Dent IBM's Prospects

To add to the woes, IBM is facing competition from Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. Increasing pricing pressure is eroding margins, and profitability has trended down over the years, barring occasional spikes. Weaknesses in its traditional business and foreign exchange volatility remain significant concerns.

IBM's frequent acquisitions have also escalated integration risks. Buyouts have negatively impacted the company's balance sheet, resulting in high levels of goodwill and net intangible assets. Moreover, a highly leveraged balance sheet has been troubling IBM over time.

title: Why Every IBM Investor Is Looking At This One Number

Why Every IBM Investor Is Looking At This One Number

The number International Business Machines (IBM) shareholders are watching comes from one business: its software. You may think of IBM as a consulting and hardware company, but its growth question lies in software. Yet over the year to November 3, 2026, IBM stock lost 16.5%, while the S&P 500 returned 11.9%. IBM's software growth sped up in fiscal Q3 2026 anyway, and that is the contradiction. So how fast is IBM's software growing now, and how much of it is new?

IBM's Software Speed-Up Came Mostly From New Business

Measured at constant currency, IBM's software revenue grew 9% in fiscal Q3 2026. That was four points faster than in Q2, management said on the October 21 call. Its high-value annual recurring revenue base, software sales that repeat each year, grew 8% to $24.9 billion.

Some of a jump like that can be borrowed from the quarter before, and IBM did close about two-thirds of the large deals that slipped out of Q2. Management, however, put those deals at about a quarter of the speed-up and called about three-quarters of it net new business. Based on management's own split, most of the gain was not catch-up.

Can IBM's Software Growth Hold As Mainframe Software Cools?

Management said not all of that growth will hold. The company does not expect transaction processing, the software that runs on its mainframes, to keep growing at double digits, and said it could perhaps moderate from Q3 into Q4. So more of the growth has to come from the rest of IBM's software, such as Red Hat, and so far Red Hat is holding up.

That matters because software license deals have already swung IBM's software growth once. In fiscal Q2 2026, management said, a double-digit fall in transactional software sales, which make up about a fifth of its software business, cut software growth by 4 to 5 points. In Q3, those sales rose by double digits, mostly in transaction processing, which grew 10%.

Red Hat looks steadier. Its revenue grew 11% in fiscal Q3 2026, the same rate as the quarter before, and its bookings growth sped up to the high teens. OpenShift, a Red Hat product, is now a $2.4 billion annual recurring revenue business, growing more than 30%.

What Would Show IBM's Software Growth Fading?

From the 9% alone, you cannot tell how much of IBM's software growth will repeat. Part of it came from deals that slipped out of Q2, and the double-digit rise in mainframe software is the part management expects to fade. If the new business does not repeat, the speed-up was a one-quarter jump. If Red Hat does not grow into the gap, IBM's software growth again swings with mainframe deals.

Factors to Note Ahead of QMCO's Q2 Earnings

On the last earnings call, management highlighted that demand remained strong across the business, supported by increasing data volumes and the need to optimize storage costs, improve infrastructure efficiency and reduce power consumption. The company reported first-quarter revenues of $80.8 million, up 25.7% year over year, driven by strong demand for ActiveScale and tape storage solutions. Management expects continued strong bookings and a substantial backlog to support second-quarter performance.

For the fiscal second quarter, Quantum expects revenues of $82 million, plus or minus $2 million, implying nearly 31% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses are projected at $27 million, plus or minus $1 million. The company anticipates non-GAAP adjusted earnings of 12 cents per share, plus or minus 10 cents, and adjusted EBITDA of $6 million (+/- $1 million).

In the last reported quarter, management highlighted increasing traction among large enterprise customers, with a significant rise in deals valued at more than $1 million during the first quarter, the majority exceeding $3 million. The company also secured a significant renewal and expansion of an ActiveScale deployment with a leading European biometrics institution in the first quarter. In the last reported quarter, management stated that customers typically expand deployments after experiencing the solution's scalability, resilience and power efficiency. Continued customer expansions and larger enterprise deals could have supported second-quarter business momentum.

The chances of a 30% jump for Accenture (ACN) stock depend mostly on whether the company keeps growing its revenue. Shares returned 50.3% between August 5 and November 3, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.7%. Even after that run, a Trefis three-year scenario built on the company's own figures models an upside of 39%. How much of that gain would come from Accenture's own business, and how much from a higher P/E?

Most Of Accenture's Upside Comes From Selling More

In the scenario, 70.9% of the gain comes from higher revenue and 31.6% comes from a higher P/E, while a slightly lower net margin takes back 2.4%. The table below sets Accenture's figures for the twelve months to August 2026 beside the scenario's figures three years on.

Most of the upside would come from Accenture selling more consulting and managed services work, not from investors paying more for each dollar of its profit.

Accenture trades at 18.3 times its trailing earnings, placing it below its average of 23.3 across its last 12 fiscal quarter-end readings. The scenario assumes a P/E of 20.3 in year three, meaning today's multiple moves 40% of the way back toward that average.

What Does Accenture Have To Keep Winning?

Accenture has to keep winning managed services work, which covers clients' applications, infrastructure and operations. Management said on the October 1, 2026 call that sales of managed services grew 8% in U.S. dollars in fiscal 2026, compared with 5% for consulting. Clients booked $84.5 billion of new work over the year, equal to 1.1 times that year's revenue. More than 400 clients started their first advanced AI work with Accenture in fiscal 2026.

Revenue grows 8.1% a year in the scenario, a quarter faster than the 6.5% growth in U.S. dollars Accenture reported for fiscal 2026. Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 3% to 6% in local currency. The scenario is the more optimistic of the two, holding its pace for three years while the guide covers one fiscal year. Of the 5% growth in local currency during fiscal 2026, management said about 3% was organic. Management also said pricing was stable over fiscal 2026, but lower in many areas of the business during the fourth quarter.
